title: Perineal Tear: Postpartum Care and Follow-Up

evidenceAudit.scope: Woman after repair of a first to fourth degree perineal tear in a Saudi hospital or primary health care centre: ward care, pain relief, ice packs, stool softeners, antibiotics after third and fourth degree tears, wound hygiene, bladder and bowel checks, pelvic floor physiotherapy, the 6 to 12 week follow-up, referral for incontinence, and counselling about the mode of birth next time. Companion to the perineal tear assessment and repair topic. Uses the Oman Ministry of Health guideline and the NSW Royal Hospital for Women business rule, which follow RCOG Green-top 29, with Saudi study data.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology guideline on follow-up after perineal tears was found; the Oman Ministry of Health guideline OBG-CLN-GUD-58 (a Gulf neighbour that follows RCOG Green-top 29) and the NSW Royal Hospital for Women business rule are used instead. The RCOG Green-top 29 full text was not re-read for this topic.

Doses differ between sources: lactulose 15 mL twice daily for 10 days to 2 weeks (Oman) versus 20 mL daily (NSW); oral antibiotics for 7 days (Oman) versus 5 days (NSW). Both are shown and the choice follows the unit protocol.

The NSW rule also lists docusate, macrogol, diclofenac, tramadol and oxycodone; only paracetamol, ibuprofen, lactulose and co-amoxiclav have a label reviewed here. Diclofenac is replaced by ibuprofen as the anti-inflammatory tablet; the dose of ibuprofen is from the over-the-counter label, not from the NSW rule.
Ice packs: the NSW rule advises 20 minutes as needed for the first 72 hours but also notes that ice packs can impede blood supply, so use with caution.
Wound swab culture and bladder scan are used in practice when infection or retention is suspected; neither guideline gives a threshold, so only the symptom triggers are written.
The follow-up interval differs: Oman advises a urogynaecology visit 6 to 12 weeks after repair; NSW advises review at 4 weeks and 4 months and pelvic floor exercises from 6 to 12 weeks.
The US acetaminophen and ibuprofen labels are over-the-counter drug facts labels; breastfeeding information was not reviewed beyond the label.
Figures were read by automated extraction of PDF and label text; spot-check each dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: A third or fourth degree tear damages the external or internal anal sphincter; early repair and protection from straining give 60 to 80% of women no symptoms at 12 months (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.3). Hard stools and straining stress the repair and raise the risk of wound breakdown, so stool softeners are given for 10 days to 2 weeks (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.1). Broad-spectrum antibiotics given at the repair reduce wound infection and breakdown (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1). Pelvic floor and sphincter muscles recover with guided exercise, so physiotherapy is started and exercises are encouraged from 6 to 12 weeks (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1). Missed or unrepaired rectal mucosa injury can later form a rectovaginal fistula (Oman MOH guideline, Section 2.1).

symptoms: Perineal pain that persists or worsens, soreness when sitting or passing stool (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.3).
Flatus, faecal soiling, faecal incontinence or urgency (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.3).
Difficulty passing urine, incontinence or urgency (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.2).
Pain with sex or sexual difficulty (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.3).
Fever, foul discharge or increasing pain at the wound (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
physicalSigns: Clean, dry, closed perineal wound with no swelling or discharge (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Wound gaping, pus, spreading redness or haematoma (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Stool or flatus passing from the vagina suggests a fistula (Oman MOH guideline, Section 2.1).
Urine retention with a full bladder (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.2).
redFlags: Wound infection or breakdown with fever or sepsis signs: same-day assessment and antibiotics (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Spreading pain, swelling or a tense, bruised perineum suggests haematoma: urgent obstetric review (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Passing stool or gas through the vagina: suspected rectovaginal fistula, refer to a specialist (Oman MOH guideline, Section 2.1).
Unable to pass urine: catheterise and review (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.2).

No bowel opening before discharge or severe constipation with pain: do not discharge until defecation has occurred unless home follow-up is arranged (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Incontinence of stool or flatus at follow-up: refer to a urogynaecologist or colorectal surgeon (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.3).
precipitants: Third or fourth degree tear, or rectal buttonhole tear (Oman MOH guideline, Section 2).
Forceps delivery, midline episiotomy and birth weight over 4 kg (Oman MOH guideline, Section 3.1).
Constipation, straining and poor wound hygiene (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Diabetes or poor healing (Annals of Saudi Medicine 2025, Results).
First vaginal birth: sphincter injury is 6.1% in first births and 1.7% in later births (Oman MOH guideline, Section 1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Fever, increasing pain, foul discharge, gaping or pus (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Severe pain, tense swelling and bruising, retention of urine (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Flatus, soiling or urgency; confirmed by endoanal ultrasonography or manometry (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.3).
Stool or gas through the vagina after an unrecognised mucosal tear (Oman MOH guideline, Section 2.1).
Unable to pass urine, leaking or urgency (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.2).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Redness, swelling, discharge, gaping or severe tenderness
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Observe lochia and the condition of the perineum daily in hospital (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Explain the injury and the plan
actions: Give a detailed explanation of the extent of the tear, the repair and the follow-up plan, with written information (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.3; NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.3).
Offer the chance to talk about the birth and ask questions (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Review by a doctor, ideally on day one after birth (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Control pain
actions: Give regular paracetamol and an anti-inflammatory tablet if there is no contraindication (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Table 1).
Use ice packs for 20 minutes as needed in the first 72 hours, with caution (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2 and Section 3.3).
Suggest a rolled towel under each thigh when sitting and feeding lying on her side (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Prevent constipation and protect the repair
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Throughout the stay and for 10 days to 2 weeks
actions: Prescribe a single-agent stool softener; do not add bulking agents (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.1; NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.3).
Encourage fluids, answering the first urge, support of the stitches with a pad when passing stool, and no straining (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Make sure the bowel has opened before discharge unless home follow-up is arranged (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Care for the wound and bladder
actions: Wash with water only, no soap, and dry gently (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Observe the perineum and lochia daily and support the perineum when coughing and sneezing (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2; Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.2).
Keep the urinary catheter at least 24 hours after sphincter repair, then check bladder function (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.1 and Section 6.2).
Complete the oral antibiotic course started at the repair (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Refer to physiotherapy
actions: Refer to the physiotherapist at the time of repair for review and pelvic floor exercises (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.2; NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1).
Encourage pelvic floor muscle contraction when standing or moving to ease pain (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Discharge safely
actions: Give written instructions on pain relief, antibiotics and stool softeners (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Give contact details for new or worrying symptoms (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
Book the follow-up visit before she leaves (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Follow up and plan future births
clinicalManagement.timeframe: 6 to 12 weeks, and early in the next pregnancy
actions: Ask about bowel, bladder, pain and sexual symptoms and examine the perineum (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.3).
Refer for endoanal ultrasonography, manometry and specialist review if she has incontinence or pain (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.3).

In a later pregnancy discuss the mode of birth early, again as needed and at about 36 weeks; offer caesarean birth if she has symptoms or a defect (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.4; NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.3).
Do episiotomy only if clinically indicated (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.4).

regimens.indication: Regular pain relief after perineal tear
regimens.dose: 1,000 mg every 6 hours regularly (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Table 1); the over-the-counter 500 mg label limits to 3,000 mg in 24 hours (Acetaminophen label, Directions). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.duration: While pain lasts, usually 1 to 2 weeks; ask a doctor if pain lasts more than 10 days (Acetaminophen label, Stop use)
adjustments: Do not take with any other acetaminophen-containing product (Acetaminophen label, Do not use).
Warfarin users should ask a doctor or pharmacist (Acetaminophen label, Ask a doctor or pharmacist).
The NSW rule dose of 4,000 mg a day is above the 3,000 mg limit on the over-the-counter label; follow the unit policy (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Table 1; Acetaminophen label, Directions).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Skin reaction: stop and seek care (Acetaminophen label, Allergy alert).
Liver injury risk with alcohol or overdose (Acetaminophen label, Liver warning).
contraindications: Allergy to acetaminophen or an inactive ingredient (Acetaminophen label, Do not use).
Liver disease: ask a doctor before use (Acetaminophen label, Ask a doctor before use).
regimens.sourceTitle: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) 500 mg tablets: US drug facts label (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Table 1; Acetaminophen label, Section Directions

regimens.indication: Added pain relief after perineal tear
regimens.patientGroup: Adult women after perineal repair with no contraindication to an anti-inflammatory
regimens.dose: 200 mg to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed, up to 1,200 mg in 24 hours (Ibuprofen label, Directions); the NSW rule uses diclofenac 50 mg every 8 hours as the regular anti-inflammatory (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Table 1). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.route: Oral with water; take with food or milk if the stomach is upset (Ibuprofen label, Directions)
regimens.duration: Shortest time possible; ask a doctor if pain lasts more than 10 days (Ibuprofen label, Stop use)
adjustments: Check a lactation reference for breastfeeding; the over-the-counter label asks to ask a health professional first (Ibuprofen label, Pregnancy or breast-feeding).
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time (Ibuprofen label, Directions).
Anti-inflammatory tablets may raise bleeding or blood pressure after birth; check the haemoglobin and blood pressure if risk factors exist (Ibuprofen label, Ask a doctor before use).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Stomach pain, black stools or vomiting blood: stop and seek care (Ibuprofen label, Stop use).
Pain that increases or is severe: examine for infection or haematoma (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.1.2).
contraindications: Previous allergic reaction to ibuprofen or other pain relievers, including aspirin-triggered asthma (Ibuprofen label, Do not use).
Right before or after heart surgery (Ibuprofen label, Do not use).
Ask a doctor first with stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, liver cirrhosis or a diuretic (Ibuprofen label, Ask a doctor before use).
regimens.sourceTitle: Ibuprofen 200 mg tablets (NSAID): US drug facts label (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Table 1; Ibuprofen label, Section Directions

regimens.indication: Stool softening to avoid straining after sphincter repair (off-label)
regimens.patientGroup: Women after repair of a third or fourth degree tear
regimens.dose: 15 mL (10 g) twice daily for 10 days to 2 weeks (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.1); the NSW rule uses 20 mL once daily (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Table 1). Dilution and preparation: none; oral solution, may be mixed with water or juice; adjust the dose to give soft stools.
regimens.route: Oral, measured with a spoon or cup (Lactulose label, Description)
regimens.duration: 10 days to 2 weeks (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.1)
adjustments: Off-label: the US label covers portal-systemic encephalopathy only; the dose is from the Oman guideline (Lactulose label, Indications).
Contains galactose and lactose; use with caution in diabetes (Lactulose label, Precautions).
Do not add bulking agents; single-agent stool softeners are advised (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Section 3.3).
Reduce the dose or stop if diarrhoea occurs (Lactulose label, Adverse Reactions).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Stool consistency and absence of straining (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.1).
Diarrhoea, bloating and fluid or electrolyte loss (Lactulose label, Adverse Reactions).
contraindications: Patients who require a low-galactose diet (Lactulose label, Contraindications).
regimens.sourceTitle: Lactulose Solution USP 10 g/15 mL: US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.1; Lactulose label, Contraindications and Precautions

regimens.indication: Completing the antibiotic course after repair of a third or fourth degree tear
regimens.patientGroup: Women after sphincter repair without severe penicillin hypersensitivity
regimens.dose: 875 mg/125 mg one tablet every 12 hours for five days (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Table 1); the Oman guideline asks for oral antibiotics to complete 7 days of treatment (Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.1). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.route: Oral, swallowed whole at the start of a meal to improve absorption of clavulanate and reduce stomach upset (Co-amoxiclav label, Dosage and Administration)
regimens.duration: 5 days (NSW) or 7 days (Oman); choose per the unit protocol
adjustments: Do not use the 875 mg/125 mg tablet if glomerular filtration rate is below 30 mL/min (Co-amoxiclav label, Dosage).
Breastfeeding: amoxicillin passes into milk; watch the infant for diarrhoea or thrush (Co-amoxiclav label, Nursing mothers).
Mild or delayed non-severe penicillin allergy: the NSW rule uses cephalexin plus metronidazole (NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Table 1).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Diarrhoea and signs of Clostridioides difficile colitis (Co-amoxiclav label, Warnings).
Liver function if prolonged or repeated (Co-amoxiclav label, Warnings).
Rash or allergy (Co-amoxiclav label, Adverse Reactions).
contraindications: History of serious hypersensitivity reaction to amoxicillin, clavulanate or other beta-lactam antibiotics (Co-amoxiclav label, Contraindications).
Previous cholestatic jaundice or liver dysfunction with amoxicillin and clavulanate (Co-amoxiclav label, Contraindications).

regimens.sourceEdition: NSW Royal Hospital for Women rule, Table 1; Oman MOH guideline, Section 6.1; Co-amoxiclav label, Section 2 and Section 4

patientEducation: Keep the area clean with water only and dry gently.
Take your pain relief and stool softener regularly.
Support the stitches with a pad when you open your bowels, and do not strain.
Do your pelvic floor exercises as your physiotherapist shows you.
Come back at once for fever, foul discharge, increasing pain, or if you cannot pass urine or stool.
Tell us about any leaking of stool or gas, even if embarrassing; it can be treated.
lifestyleAndDiet: Drink plenty of fluids and eat fibre-rich food.
Sit on a rolled towel or soft cushion.
Avoid sex until healed and comfortable.
Plan your next birth with your doctor early in pregnancy.
